thread:
jane_cs: Customer (ACME) opened INC-2042 — severe latency and region mismatch. Console shows us-west2 but their traces show requests hitting eu-west-1. Request id 02f3a7b9, timestamp 2024-11-01T15:34:12Z. Can eng take a look?

mike_oncall: Ack, looking. Can you paste the request id and any ingress logs you have? Did they set a region override?

jane_cs: They used default hosted endpoint (no explicit region param). Ingress logs (sanitized):
```
[2024-11-01T15:34:12Z] req=02f3a7b9 src=52.11.23.7 backend=eu-west-1 node=gw-03
headers:
  x-redwood-region: us-west2
  x-request-id: 02f3a7b9
response-headers:
  X-Redwood-Serving-Region: eu-west-1
  X-Redwood-Instance: model-srv-07
latency_ms: 5420
```

dan_routing: Huh — client hint says us-west2 but serving region header is eu-west-1. Could be fallback due to capacity. Any routing policy rollouts recently?

oliver_platform: We rolled out a fallback policy yesterday that allows cross-region fallback to cheaper pools for non-enterprise orgs. That could explain being served from eu-west-1, but console should still show the actual serving region (it currently shows the requested/preferred region). That's a UI mismatch.

sophia_sre: We saw a brief capacity pressure in us-west2 around 15:30Z; autoscaler throttled and fallbacks kicked in. I can confirm requests were routed to eu-west-1. We'll investigate why console and traces disagreed.

mike_oncall: Short-term mitigation: we can enable a region-pin header for the org (X-Redwood-Region-Lock: true) to force honoring the client region if they need residency. Not ideal, but could help this customer until the UI/routing bug is fixed.

oliver_platform: The console currently surfaces "Region preference" from the request object, not the server response. We need to add a "Serving region" column that reads X-Redwood-Serving-Region from traces. Filing a PL ticket.

dan_routing: Forensics note: the fallback code path sets the serving region header correctly. If the UI reads a cached preference key instead of the live trace, that'll create exactly this mismatch. Possible cache invalidation bug.

infra-bot: incident created: INC-2042 -> routing/team assigned. https://redwood.atlassian/INC-2042 :rotating_light:

oliver_platform: I'll prepare a small hotfix to surface serving_region in the console and mark it as "actual region used". Low-risk change.

sophia_sre: Also adding an alert when serving_region != requested_region for >1% of traffic over 1m, so we detect regressions earlier.

jane_cs: Customer wants root cause and ETA. Please confirm next steps so I can update them.

mike_oncall: Plan: (1) immediate mitigation: enable X-Redwood-Region-Lock for ACME (will do) (2) SRE scales us-west2 capacity (in progress) (3) Platform pushes console fix today (oliver) (4) Routing reviews fallback policy and cache invalidation (dan). ETA: mitigation 4h, full fix 24-48h. Marking P1.

oliver_platform: Console change pushed to staging, testing now. PR #4821.

dan_routing: Found root cause: cache layer was returning a stale "region_pref" for the UI because fallback responses weren't invalidating the UI cache. Pushing a patch to invalidate on fallback event.

jane_cs: :thumbsup: I'll tell the customer we have a mitigation and ETA. Post here when prod change is live.

deploy-bot: promoted console fix to prod at 2024-11-01T17:02:10Z. changelist: show-serving-region-from-trace.

oliver_platform: Prod change live. Console now shows a "Serving region" field and backfills values from traces for the last 60m.

sophia_sre: SRE: us-west2 capacity stabilized, fallback rate dropped back to baseline. Alerting rule added.

jane_cs: Customer confirms latency is back to normal. Console now shows eu-west-1 for those requests (which matches logs) — they were expecting us-west2, so I'm discussing Dedicated/private options for strict regional residency.

dan_routing: Note: hosted defaults allow fallback. If customer needs guaranteed region, propose Dedicated or Private deployments.

jane_cs: Will propose Dedicated trial. Closing loop for now. Thanks everyone.
